answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns (three ordinary rounds in each of four seasons). Courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: “each player takes twelve ordinary turns”; courtship “no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.”

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate Quarters servants to Available, then Expended to Quarters; resolve the round event; resolve applicable monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity tile; play the exact required attendees; assign service; resolve all positive favours before negatives; optionally buy; clean up. Used servants go to Expended Service, played gentry to personal discard, and the tile returns to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. The last player in turn order advances the marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity and Player Reference: “rotate service → event → ongoing effects → choose tile…”; “used servants to Expended Service; played gentry to personal discard; activity tile back…”

answers.answer: Passing order: all servants directly to Available Service; return discarded gentry to hand; resolve the event, then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free full Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; the last player advances the marker. Servants used for ongoing effects are expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: “all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.”

answers.answer: Yes. The 6.1 reputation after step 2 is the screening level for the tile and guests for the entire activity; Service Help later lowering actual reputation to 3.4 does not invalidate them. Each Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; four uses require 12 increments. It cannot take one directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed “at the end of step 2” and remains for the whole activity. Service Help: “3 increments per servant” from Quarters to Available.

answers.answer: Resolve every positive favour before any negative favour; order within either group is otherwise your choice. At minimum reputation you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to shield yourself from its consequences; losses stop at 1.1. For a guest with a money penalty, the full penalty must be payable: use available positive money favours, a money VP card or Borrow Money; borrow if short and possible. If still unable to fund it, you cannot play the guest.
answers.evidence: Hosting: “Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours”; money penalty must be “fully payable”; at minimum “cannot take a negative favour first to shelter it.”

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100; repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments per servant, move one Quarters servant to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments for a full refresh; this special action is once per turn. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and “At minimum you cannot…take a special action”; Service Help cannot take directly from Expended.

answers.answer: Use the Butler’s Room as an activity with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no hiring fee. On first use the room upgrades. Its upgraded option instead recruits one common servant (footman, valet or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service, instead of up to two from supply; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Room requires an available butler (or underbutler) and “no gentry”; hires go “into Expended Service.”

answers.answer: A housekeeper can substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room, a footman can substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler can substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet or footman) even when that type remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution conditions explicitly stated.

answers.answer: Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry; it enters Expended Service immediately. It is not immediately available: ordinarily it moves Expended → Quarters at your next service rotation, then Quarters → Available at your second subsequent rotation. Passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier; once in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can allow earlier use. Another player can never recruit it.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry: “only way to acquire an underbutler”; timing and opponent restriction stated.

answers.answer: Pay the Market space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: “space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier”; Reserve £300; minimum £100; no duplicates; reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A duplicate drawn stacks on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn; duplicates share one space. Reserve-eligible tiles go straight to Reserve and another is drawn. When filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so no refill occurs.
answers.evidence: Refill paragraph: sliding, duplicate stacking/redraw, qualifying Reserve tiles, sorting; one from a two-tile stack “causes no refill.”

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; subsequent Service draws go directly there except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and later PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. The Market is fully refreshed after each of the first three courtships as standard in this compendium.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh: movement after courtships 1 and 2; “Full refresh occurs after each of the first three courtships.”

answers.answer: At ordinary courtships 1–3, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. Score each player’s tile VP in the current face-up theme category, including negative VP and only the face-up hybrid category. Highest gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand; on a highest-score tie, each tied player draws a VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them face down at the objective deck bottom. Then open Reserve, fully refresh Market, reveal the next theme to the right of earlier themes, pass first player anticlockwise, and advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep, ordinary courtships steps 1–4 and subsequent order.

answers.answer: Final courtship returns Fairchilds and scores tile VP across all four revealed themes (a repeated category counts again, including negative VP). Highest gets a VP card and Fairchild. A tie is broken by reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards. Discard the final objective, then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible before moving to Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: Final courtship paragraph.

answers.answer: Final VP categories: face-up improvement-tile VP; gentry VP in hand and discard; fulfilled objectives; reputation; servants; wealth; retained unused VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 give 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP. Wealth gives 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Game tie-break: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position does not break a tie.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and “Ties: tied player with final Fairchild wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied share victory.”

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup and two more on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three for scoring. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase the retained total without causing extra discards. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down on the objective deck bottom. Tile objectives require ownership at game end, not an upgraded face.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: “five at setup plus two on round 6”; four courtship discards leave three; simultaneous discard and tile ownership requirements stated.

answers.answer: A VP card benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later own turn (including multiple cards), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards score their printed VP at game end; you cannot take both benefit and VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP-card use timing, destination and retained-card scoring.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip/upgrade after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined category visible and flips after every use, moving to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into a monument has its one front-side activity use, then becomes an ongoing monument and cannot host again. Hybrids count only in their currently face-up category for courtship and objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: mandatory normal upgrade, hybrid flip, suites becoming monuments; hybrid face-up category counts.

answers.answer: Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn during ongoing effects on both hosting and passing turns; no income during courtship, and a newly bought monument first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works during ongoing effects on hosting or passing: use one available servant to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant cannot serve the activity and goes to Expended at turn end. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects, monument and Servants’ Hall paragraphs.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: play one casual guest from hand, provide its normal service; one footman on the tile; double all guest favours, including negative; upgrades and remains an activity. Queen’s Suite: one prestige guest from hand, normal guest service, housekeeper on tile; double one chosen favour; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: draw one prestige guest to attend, no personal guest service, butler on tile; double nonnegative favours only; keep guest and put it in discard at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed count of one guest, which cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and fixed-count paragraph.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player. Starting with that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, each player chooses an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Use reputation counters 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max with 1 showing and Max at the bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Common wheel baseline is 1.1; actual start is Cavendish 1.4 and Asquith, Ponsonby, York 1.1. Each gets one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; tiles Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire gets 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen and 2 underbutlers total; no butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants are returned to the box and are unavailable this game, so they cannot be hired later.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6 gives per-player counts and says unused servants are unavailable this game.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from casual deck, shuffle them, and deal two to each player’s hand. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules; they are not a separate guest type in play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4 and Gentry section: “Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon.”

answers.answer: For four players, select one per player plus one: five double-sided monuments. Select at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze, so both cannot be selected. Put selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles in the bag. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments also go in the bag and do not count against the selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Fill six different eligible Market spaces with tiles of PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set aside ineligible draws and return them to the bag after filling; stack eligible duplicates in the matching space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort spaces by ascending printed sorting number, starting at £300. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Set Alderley Hall to its standard side with the round marker at 1; put one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately. Reveal the first theme face up for open courtship; revealed themes remain in order through the game rather than leaving play. Place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9: marker, reminder tokens, separately shuffled decks, first theme revealed/open, themes kept in order, Fairchilds face up.

answers.answer: During hosting rotation, move the servant in Quarters to Available first; then move the servant in Expended to Quarters. Each advances exactly one space and the Expended servant is not moved twice. An unused servant already in Available remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1 and ordinary rotation table.

answers.answer: Yes, you may host the Private Study activity later that turn if legal, but it does not earn the Village Fair reward immediately: the event checks whether the Study is already upgraded when the event resolves, before you choose/host it. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and two reputation, on standard spaces 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Round events table (3 and 9; no reward if not upgraded at this step); Private Study paragraph (upgraded side reward only on Village Fair).

answers.answer: The event resolves before ongoing tile effects: during hosting after service rotation; during passing after servants and discarded gentry return. On standard space 6, draw two objectives and keep both secret with your others. Passing players receive the event too because round-track events resolve on passing turns.
answers.evidence: Round-track event order and standard event table; “Draw Objectives” on space 6; events occur on each player’s turn including pass.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so low-reputation players may play higher-PR ones. All other requirements still apply, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table: National Holiday ignores PR “still obey all other requirements, including service and gentry counts/types.”

answers.answer: Yes, buy any number from Market and/or Reserve within funds. Complete all purchases before sliding/refilling, at the unchanged market prices that applied before the sequence; each tile keeps its original space price or £300 Reserve price plus modifier. No special-action or VP-card refresh between purchases. These same unchanged-market and no-refresh-between-purchases rules apply to both Builders’ Holiday and Market Purchase VP-card benefits; refill all empty spaces together afterward.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; they cannot reappear in that refresh. Leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six spaces under normal rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix.
answers.evidence: Refresh paragraph: set all Market tiles aside, Reserve unchanged, refill, “then return the set-aside tiles to the bag.”

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment; crossing position 5 to 1 raises a level and crossing 1 to 5 lowers one. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); ignore losses beyond minimum. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you may take special actions before or in the middle of resolving a reputation favour to make room.
answers.evidence: Reputation section: each symbol is one increment; boundary crossings, bounds and Max.5 excess rules stated.

answers.answer: Money is public, players may not give or receive money between them, and never spend more than you have. The money supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed. Costs requiring penalties must be fully payable; if short, borrow if possible, and if still unable to fund it you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Money held is public; no transfers; “Money supply is unlimited (use proxies if needed)”; penalty must be fully payable.

answers.answer: Family members can fill ladies/gentlemen requirements: Ladies means all female family/guest cards and Gentlemen all male family/guest cards. They cannot fill “casual guest” requirements, which exclude family. You must meet the exact printed number and type; no extra or fewer gentry. Family requires no personal service and has no PR.
answers.evidence: Invite Gentry section: exact counts/types; definitions of Ladies/Gentlemen; casual/prestige exclude family; family no personal service; family cards have no PR.

answers.answer: For an ordinary invite favour, draw the indicated guest from its deck, reveal it to everyone and add it to your hand; it does not attend the current activity. For screening, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand; put rejected cards on the bottom of the corresponding guest deck without revealing them.
answers.evidence: Gentry invite table and screening procedure.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss anyone. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, the current activity or discard, including one just drawn by an earlier favour. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the dismissed guest on the bottom of its matching guest deck; it is no longer yours, will not return on passing, and does not score.
answers.evidence: Dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose either screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lord and Dowager give their stated benefits; Lady and Heir offer choices, with dismissal itself optional.
answers.evidence: Base family card favour table.

answers.answer: The bonus applies only if a male prestige guest attends. A male casual guest and a female prestige guest do not qualify; Charles Fairchild does qualify because he is a male prestige guest. The Young Lady still draws one casual guest, and gains two reputation in the qualifying case.
answers.evidence: Family favours table: Young Lady draws one casual guest and gains two reputation if male prestige attends; Charles explicitly qualifies.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are guests, not family, and have no family dismissal immunity; either may be dismissed under the ordinary guest rule.
answers.evidence: Gentry section specifies gender, type, PR, service, favours and dismissal immunity.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. A player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gossip cards paragraph and minimum-reputation protection.

answers.answer: A Barn earns one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing earns none.
answers.evidence: Barn: “every time you host an Estate activity, gain one reputation”; no reward for owning/pass.

answers.answer: Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available and then all Expended servants to Quarters. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available; it cannot take from Expended. The Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant directly from Quarters each ordinary turn after rotation, without reputation cost, in addition to Available servants; the used servant goes to Expended at turn end.
answers.evidence: Service mechanisms table and Servants’ Quarters tile paragraph.

answers.answer: The front Private Study requires a butler and exactly two family members; it has no tile favour. Once upgraded, it becomes an ongoing tile and cannot be hosted again. Its ongoing reward is £300 plus two reputation on Village Fair rounds (spaces 3 and 9), without staffing or hosting.
answers.evidence: Private Study paragraph: activity requirements and upgraded ongoing effect.

answers.answer: Before upgrade, Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. After upgrade it uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. The extra objective adds to the number retained for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph.

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one and puts the other on the bottom of the objective deck. It adds one retained objective for final scoring; it does not trigger an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table and objectives paragraph: gives one additional retained objective; extra objectives do not cause extra discard.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available, including those in Expended Service, and they can be used immediately. Service Help instead costs 3 increments per servant, moves one servant from Quarters to Available, and cannot take directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table contrasts Refresh Service and Service Help.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire (not an underbutler) into Expended Service. It is not immediately available to provide service through this hire alone; a Refresh Service VP card can make servants in Expended immediately available.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Hire Servant destination and underbutler exclusion; Expended servants advance only one space at rotation.

answers.answer: Yes. Return one gentry card, including a family member, from your personal discard to hand. If done before Invite Gentry, you may select that returned card to attend the activity if it meets the normal requirements; returning it does not itself play it.
answers.evidence: Refresh Guest benefit paragraph.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Ordinary servant scoring gives 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The separate ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP servant row.

answers.answer: Yes. An upgraded Queen’s Suite counts as a monument and an Estate tile; an upgraded Lionheart Suite counts as a monument and a Prestige tile, so each qualifies for its category objective and the monument objective. Hybrids count only in the currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference explicitly covers both suites and hybrid category counting.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. Tile ownership at game end is enough; tiles need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference group list and ownership rule.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective scores 1 VP per prestige guest; the every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests, including a final Fairchild as prestige guest. Only each complete group of three scores; an incomplete group scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Objective reference: “1 VP per prestige guest” and “per complete three guests (all nonfamily guests)”; final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest.

answers.answer: The reputation objective gives 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective gives 10 VP for at least £1200. Wheel position does not affect ordinary reputation VP or reputation tie resolution; reputation VP depends on level and ties use level.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP/tie rules.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. The unupgraded tile draws one prestige guest. The upgraded side draws one prestige guest and optionally dismisses one to four guests from hand, current activity or discard to the bottom of their decks. It remains an activity tile; it does not become an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal discard-pile limit. Gentry in the discard pile remain yours and score normally; passing returns them to hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: “There is no hand or discard-pile limit”; discard-pile gentry score normally.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; there is no top-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve: “Every Reserve tile is public”; inspect all and buy any one, including underneath another.

answers.answer: You are not required to host when you could. If the preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 5: without all required gentry/service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity possible, must pass. Passing is an available turn choice.

answers.answer: Yes. On a pass you may take the free Market refresh benefit, the paid Refresh Market special action, and Market Refresh VP-card benefits, including multiple VP cards in the same turn. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action refresh; pass and VP-card refreshes have separate availability.
answers.evidence: Special action paragraph: free pass and VP refreshes do not use the once-per-turn special refresh allowance; multiple Market Refresh VP cards may be used.

answers.answer: No, these special actions are not interrupts during another player’s turn. They are available at any time on your own turn, whether hosting or passing, with sufficient reputation to pay.
answers.evidence: Special actions: “available at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing.”

answers.answer: The printed guest-invite favour is mandatory unless expressly optional, so you cannot decline an ordinary casual-guest invite while resolving the activity’s other favours. An optional dismissal is different: dismissal is always optional, and you may choose an eligible guest from hand, the current activity or discard, including a newly drawn guest.
answers.evidence: Favours are mandatory unless expressly optional; ordinary invite procedure and dismissal paragraph (“Dismissal is always optional”).
